## 0. One-paragraph summary
Landstalker (Mega Drive) is statically recompiled to C (genrecomp + Genesis Plus GX runtime) and plays on the user's Steam Deck: boot, title, intro, Massan village, dialogue, shops, church save (`.srm`), inn map, sound, controller all work.
Done so far: timing model fixed (was ~40 frames ahead of the real core), ref-vs-rec comparison tool chain, differential instruction fuzz (found real translation bugs), the Massan NPC bug (bogus function start `$017CC0`, verified fixed on the Deck), display pipeline (scaling + CRT filter), a widescreen experiment (352/384/416 px), and the doc tooling (symbols/unknowns/check_docs). The user has no programming background and the Deck is the only test machine: everything is built by Claude and verified by the user playing.

**The repository is PUBLIC** (checked 2026-10-16: unauthenticated GitHub API says public, release downloads work without login); older entries below that still talk about 'private' were corrected.

## 0a340. 2026-11-08 late (Deck, Opus 5.5 lead; dev 6d3139d, headless, USER TEST OPEN): REAL 3D LIGHT SHAPES stage 1 + 2 (model buffer, key shadow map; GPU only)
What was built: `tools/patch_lights.py` marker LK_LTMODEL v1: `mesh_tris()` reads every OBJ of a `mesh` op into triangles with smooth normals (faces within 35 deg averaged, back-facing triangles get flipped normals) -> C tables lk_lt_mtri%d / lk_lt_mtris / lk_lt_mtrin; indoors (no sun) `lk_lt_finebuild` marks each sub column a model stamps as model owned (lk_lt_mown), ground below the model lk_lt_mg = the op's "floor" if given (ship: sea -22) else min(ground, model bottom) (NOT the game's cell height: under the ship that is the DECK = collision), model bottom lk_lt_mb (bottom above mg + 4 = floating part, air below). `tools/patch_gpulight.py` marker LK_GLMODEL v1: fine texture got a 5th plane (296 x 1480; rows 1184..1479: r owned, g bottom - ground clamped 0..255, b/a ground); `lk_gl_mlist()` = the room's model triangles; at a new room world (lk_g5_bind) `lk_gm_render()` rasterizes them into a MODEL BUFFER (2048 x 1024 texture, left half, FBO + depth renderbuffer, texture unit 11, uniforms mdl / uMo / uMdl): picture space U = x - y + 1184, V = (x + y)/2 - z, orthographic along the view ray (1,1,1), depth = -z, texel z*8+32768 (r/g) + octahedral normal (b/a). The indoor view ray returns the model surface when reached before any field hit: face 1 if normal z > 0.94 else NEW FACE CODE 20 with the real normal (globals gN / gMB; FNX/FNY/new FNZ read gN for code 20; room A gets the nearest old code via fclassic() so the light pass and CPU readers never see 20). STAGE 2 (key light): SHADOW MAP of the models along lk_lt_sd (right half of the same texture; s = p.e1, t = p.e2, depth = p.d; up to 4 texels per unit; redrawn on world or direction change; uniforms uSm / uE1 / uE2); keyShare = field march WITHOUT the model's own sub columns / slabs / halo (global gKM) + smvis() (blocker search 5x5, then 7x7 filter, width = blocker distance * horizontal part of d / kpen, bias 1.5). AO with models: floating model sub columns are air down to the ground (aoh2), near a model the 4 sub column heights are interpolated (aohm), the ground below a model counts like water for the depth darkening (the ship's deck cells gave 16 unit stairs on the sea). Ship recipe `remake/recipes/proxy_ship_493.py`: side rail logs over the tapering bow (y 744..784) now sit on the deck (z 32..44), the old boxes down to z 0 stuck out of the slanted bow side = vertical light streak ('harte Kanten'); `data/proxies/ship_493.obj` rebuilt (118 faces). Test aids: LANDSTALKER_LT_MODEL=0 (off), LANDSTALKER_LT_MODELSM=0 (stage 1 only), LANDSTALKER_GL5_MODELDBG=1/2/3..9. Checked headless (81 frames 2840..3320): Lighting Off bit exact, HIDE=0 = old within the run-to-run noise (HUD hearts / sparkles differ between two identical runs too), On: the shadows stay whole (tools: /tmp scripts, `tools/lightshots.sh`). ## 0a183. 2026-10-30 morning (Deck, Opus 5.5 lead + Sonnet 5.5 agents): NATIVE PACE = ROOM 5 / ROOM 23 SLOW MOTION FIXED (USER: 'passt'). User insight: 'wir wollen ja gar keine CPU mehr nachbauen, sondern nativ laufen' -> instead of the planned +25 % overclock (0a182 option 2, SUPERSEDED) we hold the clock: `tools/patch_nativepace.py` (commit 60e24dc, marker `LK_NATIVEPACE v1`, v2 in 617875f). In `bus_advance_inner`'s line loop, when the next line would be the VBlank line and bit 7 of `g_InterruptFlags $FF0F8B` (wait bit, set by `WaitUntilVBlank $000B5E`) is still clear, the clock stays at the end of the last visible line (the extra 68K cycles are NOT counted) until the main loop reaches `WaitUntilVBlank`; cap `LANDSTALKER_NATIVEPACE_CAP` lines (default 262 = one frame) per frame, then VBlank anyway (safety for waits without the bit / room loads). `LANDSTALKER_NATIVEPACE_STAT=1` prints `nativepace: 60 frames, held H, extra lines L, cap hit C` per second. Only in the own timing mode (`LANDSTALKER_TIMING=gpgx` ignores it). Default Off = bit exact. Why 'native': our recompiled code is far faster than a real 68K, the only limit is the COUNTED cycle budget per frame; holding the clock gives the game the time it would have had on faster hardware without emulating anything more. MEASURED headless (harness `/tmp/np`: copy of `save_20261030_0318.srm`, first 300 frames of `rec_20261030_0318.txt` + idle, `LANDSTALKER_QSAVE=1 LANDSTALKER_QSREQ=l600`, hold left from 800, `--ram-dump :1`): baseline dx per frame `2 2 2 0 2 0 2 2 ...` (about 1 frame in 5 without movement); Native Pace: 2 every frame (a 0 is always compensated by a 4). Room 5 holds 7..21 frames per second, ~10-20 extra lines each, no cap hits in the room (cap hits only around the quick load). Long recording `rec_20261029_1729` (43 201 frames) with Native Pace: no crash / hang, 2 min 52 s headless; 32 of 720 seconds had cap hits (not investigated: probably loads / fades / waits without the wait bit); the replay diverges on purpose (timing changed). ## 0a182. 2026-10-30 night (Deck, Opus 5.5): ROOM 5 ROOT CAUSE = REAL CPU OVERLOAD (dropped game loop passes); MY LAG COUNTER MISCLASSIFIED THEM. Method: `GENRECOMP_CALLTRACE=lo:hi` and count frames that contain an entry of `ProcessFloorType $00603C` (called once per GameLoop pass) and of `WaitUntilVBlank $000B5E`: in room 5 some frames have NEITHER (820, 824, 826, 835, ...) = the pass ran over a whole frame. The VBlank handler `HandleVBlankInterrupt $0011DE` always clears bit 7 of `$FF0F8B` (the wait bit), so these are genuine overload frames; `LANDSTALKER_LAGSTAT` put them into 'lag_display_off' (385..397 of ~2 000 room 5 frames = ~19 %) because the game turns the display OFF during its fast uploads while the main loop still runs, and I had treated display-off as 'loading / fade'. FIX NEEDED in `tools/patch_lagstat.py`: count display-off frames with the wait bit clear as lag unless a room load / fade is running (e.g. only exclude them when the room number changed within the last N frames, or count passes directly). Numbers (headless, quick load into room 5, walking): game loop passes in frames 720..999: **241 / 280 normal (14 % lost), 254 / 280 with `LANDSTALKER_VDPWAIT=0` (9 % lost)**; frames 815..858: 34 / 44 with WIDE 19 + TALL 1, 37 / 44 with WIDE 0 / TALL 0 or WIDE 0 + TALL 1 (the wide strips cost a little). So the phase 2 VDP option DOES help (about a third of the lost frames), and the earlier 'no benefit' conclusion of TIMING_PLAN section 16 was wrong (it rested on the misclassifying counter). NEXT (user decides): (1) fix the counter and re-measure all rooms; (2) [SUPERSEDED by 0a183: Native Pace] a 'faster CPU' option (`LANDSTALKER_OVERCLOCK`, e.g. +25 % 68K cycles per frame: scale the block charge in `bus_advance`, off by default = bit exact) which should remove the room 5 slowdown completely; (3) both as options in the menu, user judges the feel; (4) check why WIDE 19 costs passes (the extra strip loads should be free, LESSONS 11 / 14).

## 0a166. 2026-10-29 night (Deck, Sonnet 5.5, on `dev`): FRIDAY'S WAKE-UP FLASH is back in the own renderer. User report: after the waterfall (room 593, Nigel wakes in bed) Friday's blinking screen effect was missing. Cause: `UpdateFridayAnimation_Flash $0037EE` (state `g_FridayAnimState $FF114B` = $41 / $42, counter $1F..$3B) writes CRAM colours 0 and 15 of line 0 straight through the VDP data port (0x0EEE (colour) on even counters, 0 on odd) and never touches the game's palette copies; the own renderer takes its palette from game RAM (LESSONS 9.w), so it never saw it. Fix (narrow, `tools/patch_own.py` end of `lk_o_palette`, comment `LK_OWN FLASH v1`): while the state is $41 / $42 the two colours come from the chip's CRAM (whatever it holds, so exact). A general rule (any directly written CRAM entry) was NOT tried: other effects (warp pad, fades) also write CRAM directly and the own palette code has special cases for them. Verified: `rec_20261029_1729` frames 23740..23790, own (`LANDSTALKER_OWN=2`) vs chip (`LANDSTALKER_OWN=0 LANDSTALKER_OWN_NOCHIP=0`): WIDE 0 = 51 / 51 frames pixel identical; WIDE 19 = same 1368 px residual on every frame as BEFORE the flash (HUD rows 5..20 + a 2 px column at the right edge, also at frame 23740) plus a 3x5 px block at the wide right margin top (x 336..338, y 0..4) on the odd flash frames only (chip white, own black; not in the 320 picture). Compare mode (`NOCHIP=0`, pre vs post, per frame): rec_20261029_1729 sum 65 878 483 -> 64 967 096 (28 frames better, e.g. 50058 -> 1520 differing px, none worse; the new log is one line short at frame 27450, not investigated, probably an interleaved console line), `rec_20261012_2204` (death / revive, also has the flash) 2 997 272 -> 153 508 (126 frames better); `rec_20261012_2057`, `_2148`, `rec_20261016_0039`, `_1338` (tree warp), `_2127` (warp pad) all identical per frame. ## 0a120. 2026-10-26 (Deck, Sonnet 5.5, on `dev`): MULTI-ROM / LANGUAGES PLAN (user: 'step 1 Unterstuetzung Europa-ROM und Sprachversionen fuer USA und EU mit Textlayer, spaeter direkte Unterstuetzung der DE-ROM'; reason: German players will NOT own the US ROM, 2 ROMs per player makes no sense). ROMs lie next to the US one in `/home/deck/Documents/NonSteamGames/landstalker/` (US `landstalker.md`, Europe, Germany `...Die Schatze von Konig Nolo (Germany).md`, Japan, Landstalker Remix v1.0). BYTE COMPARISON vs US: EUROPE 6874 bytes = header (region, checksum), 50 Hz timing constants (title `$0399F9` area, credits `$09EC20..$09ECFB`, a 7 KB credits block `$09ED49-$0A08A9`), 2 bytes at `$11EA67/93`: same layout and code = nearly the US game. GERMANY 218 409 bytes (same size / layout, but ~35 700 bytes in 1169 real code routines incl. 1-byte jump table entries `j_*`, plus ~168 000 bytes data / text / tables): a different program revision, a real second port (match routines by opcode sequences ignoring addresses, later). JAPAN 73 % / REMIX 67 % different, data shifted: no direct way. STEPS: (1a) Europe ROM as a base (build in a SEPARATE clone `~/Project-Friday-Test/ProjectL_eu`, NEVER in `~/ProjectL`: `build.sh` writes `.deps`, `src/recomp`, `build/` in the tree; `firstrun.py` `KNOWN_ROMS` only knows the US SHA-1, add the EU one only after the test); (1b) text layer + Options > Language (shipped translation files without ROM content, Deutsch first; German ROM only as an optional text source); (2, later) German ROM as a base. EUROPE TEST (1a) DONE in `~/Project-Friday-Test/ProjectL_eu` (separate clone, origin removed; US tree untouched): `build.sh` ran through with the EU ROM (SHA-1 `9fbadc86...`) without changes, no interpreter fallback; headless with `~/Project-Friday-Test/intro.txt` (6000 frames, isolated HOME, ROM copies in /tmp) the EU build shows the SAME room sequence at the SAME frames as the US build (139 at 661, 140 at 1501, 141 at 3001, 142 at 3841). CAUSE (measured: `LANDSTALKER_WAV` over 600 frames = 2 123 832 bytes EU vs 1 761 216 US = 882 vs 735 samples per frame): the core auto-detects region from the header, 'E' = PAL 50 Hz, while the platform paces 60 frames / s -> 20 % too fast (music AND game). FIRST FIX (region forced to USA) was WRONG: the EU ROM has its own `RegionCheck $11EA64` (compares the version register `$A10001` bits 7 / 6 with `$C0`; the US ROM with `$80`) and showed 'developed for use only with PAL and French SECAM Mega Drive systems'. FIX `tools/patch_region.py` v2/v3: only `config.vdp_mode = 1` + `config.master_clock = 1` (the sound chips also ran on the PAL clock: ~0.9 % more samples per frame) (video standard NTSC / 60 Hz for every ROM), the region stays auto-detected so the version register still says Europe; `LANDSTALKER_PAL=1` = auto-detect; identical for the US ROM. USER CONFIRMED the EU build after the region fix (v3): no region message, 'sieht gut aus, musik hoert sich richtig an' (short play, intro). ## 5. Root causes found (do not re-learn). Older ones: DEBUGGING.md "ROOT CAUSE" sections.
Older (previous sessions): script code with inline data (seeded via `script_tables.py`), computed-jump tables, GPGX FM buffer overrun (`patch_fmclamp`), GPGX `m68k_set_irq_delay` executing a stale instruction (`patch_irqdelay`), no SRAM persistence (`patch_sram`), READ_WORD endianness in bus.c.
This session:
1. **Timing**: only bus accesses cost cycles. Now `patch_timing.py`: `bus_add_cycles(N)` per basic block from Musashi's `m68ki_cycles` table, dynamic Bcc/DBcc/Scc/shift/MOVEM/MUL/DIV like Musashi, DRAM refresh 2/128, IRQ entry 44.
2. **68K-bus DMA stall**: GPGX's control-port write handler halts the 68K (`m68k.cycles = dma_endCycles`) with the display-state rate and a clock that may run lines ahead -> single 187,611-cycle stalls (384 lines) every other frame during text boxes (text crawled, music crackled, `clamped`). `bus_finish_dma` now restores the pre-write clock and charges the transfer at the blanking rate (also when the whole DMA ran inside the register write).
3. **Absolute short addresses** (`($XXXX).w`) are sign-extended on the 68000 (`$D192.w` = `$FFFFD192`); the generator used them unsigned (read ROM instead of RAM). `patch_absw.py`.
4. **Macro temporaries shadowing**: generator temporaries `_s/_d/_t` collided with the macros' locals in CMPM/ABCD/SBCD/NBCD (`uint8_t _s = (uint8_t)(_s)`). Also: ASL was LSL (V flag), ROX carry for count multiples of width+1, capstone mis-decodes `roxr.b Dx,Dy`, MOVEM with absolute/indexed/pc EAs was skipped, `divs` of `$80000000/-1` raised SIGFPE. `patch_insnfix.py`.
5. **Bogus function start `$017CC0`** (a seed copied from the interpreter log) lay in the middle of `btst.b #6,$48(a5)` at `$017CBE`, so `$017CAA` ended after the btst and fell through into garbage: the +X (south-east) walking block of the NPC step `$017B50` skipped the movement and the sprite-collision call. Dog and chicken therefore walked through the fence/church to the south-east. The other three directions were fine (funcdiff: 0 mismatches). The seed existed because the *generated code itself* fell through to `$017CC0` and the interpreter logged it - a circular artefact. (Fix verified on the Deck 2026-10-10.)
6. Reference-comparison pitfalls (each cost hours): `genrecomp_ref` did not load the save (diverged at frame 160); dumps were taken at different points of the frame; the replay `massan.txt` was recorded with the old timing; the two cores initialise work RAM differently (`$FF0000-09` etc. differ forever, not a bug); stack leftovers (`$FF80-$FFB3`) and a few timer words differ (44 bytes stable difference from frame ~119); NPC walking directions are random and legitimately differ between runs (the RNG does not come from the HV counter).

## 6. Entity/NPC/map facts -> moved to `docs/FORMATS.md` (single place for data and struct layouts; symbols in symbols.json)

## 7. FRAGILE: widescreen map-frame detection (added 2026-10-10)
Widescreen margins are blanked on every frame that is not the game map. "Is map" = `UpdateSprites` ($0178C8) ran within the last 4 frames or is still on the call stack (cutscene scripts), or text box / WarpToRoom on the stack, + 30-frame hold. This is a heuristic and may misclassify screens we have not looked at (dialogue, shops, inn map, cutscenes). Before touching widescreen again read DEBUGGING.md "Widescreen: map-frame detection" (assumptions, symptoms table, overrides `LANDSTALKER_WIDE_MAP=auto|always|never|auto:N`, `LANDSTALKER_WIDE_DEBUG=1`, re-verify checklist). Update: dialogues were found NOT to call UpdateSprites; rule extended (UpdateSprites recent OR `$028FD8` on the call stack, see the evidence table in DEBUGGING.md). Status of the checklist: dialogue/menu/fade verified by log only; shops, signs, chests, inn map, cutscenes NOT yet checked on the Deck.
